title: [RAWTHROW][10] torch/csrc/jit: 744 findings down to four subdirectories
body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.15.0) (oldest at bottom):
* #195859
* #195858
* __->__ #195764

## Author Notes

Ignoring most of the torchscript runtime stuff as it is slated for deletion anyways.

## Agent Notes

Written by Claude Code:

> Replaces the blanket `torch/csrc/jit/**` exclude with four subdirectory
> entries. 744 findings become 410, and seven of the eleven jit
> subdirectories clear outright. Almost all of the drop is one allow-list
> decision. The 31 findings in those seven subdirectories break down as 24
> conversions, 5 covered by the new allow-list entries, one stale file-level
> marker deleted, and one throw kept with a new line-scoped reason.
>
> **The linter change is the part to review.** `ErrorReport` is the
> TorchScript frontend's error type and accounts for 298 of the 744. It is
> built from a `SourceRange`/`TreeRef`/`Token` and carries the compilation
> call stack, so `what()` points at the user's Python source -- `TORCH_CHECK`
> stamps the C++ file and line instead, which is a different diagnostic, so
> it meets the "no TORCH_CHECK can stand in for it" bar. But allow-listing it
> alone does nothing, because the idiom is
>
>     throw ErrorReport(loc) << "..." << name << "...";
>
> and `is_allowed` required the constructor call to be the *entire* operand.
> That guard exists to stop laundering (`throw py::key_error(m).with_context(x)`),
> so I widened it as narrowly as I could: after the constructor call, a `<<`
> chain is now accepted, nothing else. That is sound here because
> `operator<<(const ErrorReport&, const T&)` returns `const ErrorReport&`, so
> `throw Foo(loc) << a << b` still throws a `Foo`; a trailing `.member()` or
> `->member()` could return anything and is still rejected. If you would
> rather this were its own PR ahead of the conversions, say so and I will
> split it.
>
> Four more allow-list entries, each caught by name -- I checked rather than
> assumed: `JITException` (by the translator in `torch/csrc/Exceptions.h`, so
> a scripted `raise` keeps its Python type), `RecursiveMethodCallError`
> (`frontend/sugared_value.h`, twice), `ObjectAttributeError`
> (`python/script_init.cpp`, three times) and `c10::BackendRuntimeException`
> (`mobile/module.cpp`, `mobile/interpreter.cpp`).
>
> The 24 conversions are mostly `std::runtime_error` -> `TORCH_CHECK` in
> `serialization/export.cpp` (5), `testing/file_check.cpp` (6), the lexer and
> a few one-offs. Four deserve a sentence each:
>
> - `mobile/model_tracer/tracer.cpp` did `catch (std::exception& ex) { ...
>   throw ex; }`, which slices the derived type and its message off. Now a
>   bare `throw;`. This is a bug fix, not a conversion.
> - `backends/xnnpack/xnnpack_graph_builder.cpp` had `throw std::exception();`
>   immediately above a `TORCH_CHECK(false, "The node of ", ..., " is not
>   supported yet")`. The check was unreachable, so its message never
>   appeared; dropping the throw makes it the live diagnostic. That also
>   removes one of the files from the plan's section 3.4 carve-out list.
> - `ir/ir.h`'s three `IRAttributeError` sites become `TORCH_CHECK` with the
>   message the constructor built, verbatim. `IRAttributeError` derives from
>   `std::exception`, has no state beyond the message and is caught by name
>   nowhere, so it did not qualify for the allow list. It now has no throw
>   site left; I have not deleted the class, because `ir/attributes.h` is an
>   installed header and that is a separate call.
> - `ir/ir.cpp` keeps `throw er;` with a line-scoped reason. `er` is exactly
>   `ErrorReport`, built by the twenty lines above it, so the copy is the
>   report and nothing is sliced.
>
> `mobile/promoted_prim_ops.cpp` and `frontend/lexer.cpp` use
> `TORCH_CHECK_INDEX`, preserving `IndexError` on the two `std::out_of_range`
> sites. No Python-visible exception type changes.
>
> **The C++-visible type does change, and it broke two in-tree callers.**
> `c10::Error` derives from `std::exception` but not from
> `std::runtime_error`, and `frontend/lexer.h` sits on the schema-parsing path
> that every `TORCH_LIBRARY` registration and `torch::jit::parseSchema` call
> reaches. Two places caught the old type by name:
>
> - `test/cpp/jit/test_misc.cpp` asserted
>   `::testing::Throws<std::runtime_error>`; now `c10::Error`.
> - `benchmarks/static_runtime/test_utils.cc` used
>   `catch (const std::runtime_error&)` as *control flow* -- it tries to parse
>   the source as TorchScript and falls back to treating it as IR text when
>   that throws. The fallback silently stopped firing, which would have taken
>   out roughly 294 tests in `static_runtime_test`, a job that runs in CI. It
>   now catches `std::exception`.
>
> Both were found by a local pre-submit review, not by the build, because
> `BUILD_TEST=0` here. Out-of-tree extensions catching `std::runtime_error`
> around a schema parse get no such patch; that is worth knowing even though
> the plan's section 3.3 only reasons about the Python boundary.
>
> **On tensorexpr.** The plan (section 3.6, and its resolved-decisions table)
> says NNC gets a *permanent* "dead code, scheduled for removal" exclude. I
> did not do that, because both halves are false. It is compiled
> unconditionally -- all 43 `build_variables.bzl` entries are in
> `core_sources_full` with no `USE_*` gate. It is reachable by default:
> `texpr_fuser_enabled_ = true`, `gpu_fuser_enabled = true`, so a plain
> `torch.jit.script` model on CUDA runs NNC-generated code with no flags, and
> it is the only TorchScript fuser left now that nvFuser's bindings are
> warning-only stubs. Static Runtime (`runtime/static/te_wrapper.cpp`) and
> `passes/mkldnn_rewrite.cpp` link it regardless of that flag. And removal is
> not scheduled: there is no deprecation notice, no tracking issue, a live
> merge rule named `NNC` with two named approvers, and recent commits keeping
> it building against LLVM 23 and 24. Its four domain exception types
> (`malformed_input` and friends, 207 of the 294) are bare
> `std::runtime_error` subclasses that only prepend a fixed string -- no
> state, caught by name nowhere, same Python type -- so allow-listing them
> would be suppression wearing a disguise. It gets a temporary burn-down
> entry worded for what it actually is, and its own PR.
>
> Test Plan:
>
> ```
> spin lint -- --take RAWTHROW --all-files
> spin lint -- --take CLANGFORMAT,RAWTHROW,NEWLINE,SPACES,TABS,TOML,RUFF,MYPY <changed>
> CMAKE_GENERATOR=Ninja USE_DISTRIBUTED=1 USE_CUDA=0 BUILD_TEST=0 \
>     pip install -e . -v --no-build-isolation
> ```
>
> All clean, and the jit tree goes to 410 findings, all inside the four
> remaining excludes. The build caught one real mistake worth recording:
> rewriting
> `FAIL_EXPORT` to pass `name` as its own `TORCH_CHECK` argument does not
> compile, because call sites pass `"literal" + node->kind().toDisplayString()`
> and `toDisplayString()` returns `const char*`. It only ever worked because
> the macro spliced `name` into a chain whose leftmost operand was a
> `std::string`. The macro keeps that shape.
>
> The linter's own behaviour was checked directly rather than only through
> its output: `is_allowed` still rejects `ErrorReport(loc).release()`,
> `py::key_error(m).with_context(x)`, `std::runtime_error(m)`, and
> `ErrorReport` outside `torch/csrc/jit/`, while accepting
> `ErrorReport(loc) << ...`.
>
> This change was authored with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code).
